newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Avmin bids for Zambia copper crown jewels.
newsitem.headline: Avmin bids for Zambia copper crown jewels.

text.p: South African mining house Avmin Ltd looked set to secure the heart of Zambia's copper industry on Friday after leading a consortium bid for the prized Nchanga and Nkana divisions accounting for half of national output, industry analysts said.

The Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) said Avmin bid for the key working assets of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) in a consortium with Phelps Dodge Corp, Noranda Inc and the Commonwealth Development Corp.

Four other concerns also bid for parts of the package "A" comprising Nkana and Nchanga -- Metorex, Straits Resources, the Binani Group and Sterlite Industries (India) Ltd. But analysts said Avmin looked well-placed to secure the deal.
Opening the bids, ZPA chief executive Valentine Chitalu said:
"Bids will be considered by our advisers, the ZCCM board, the ZPA board, and finally by the government. They will be finally approved by the cabinet."
The Zambian government hopes the privatisation of ZCCM -- which accounts for about 90 percent of Zambia's foreign earnings -- will turn around the country's economy.
Avmin, the minerals division of Anglovaal Ltd, has already won the right to develop the Konkola North copper reserve.

Nchanga and Nkana produced 225,000 tonnes of copper in the last financial year, roughly half of ZCCM's total output. The divisions include several open pit and underground copper mines, a copper tailings treatment plant, a concentrator and a cobalt treatment plant and smelter.
Mining analysts said that if the bid succeeded Avmin could have, via direct and indirect control, about 33 percent of ZCCM's assets.
This includes the right to develop the Konkola North deposit, which is estimated to be worth $500 million.
Earlier this month a consortium led by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said it was prepared to buy a majority shareholding in Zambia's Konkola Deep copper mine.

Mining analysts believe the Zambian mining industry could be set for a renaissance following privatisation with production set to surge over the next 15 years to more than a million tonnes of copper a year from around 400,000 at present.

Development of the two Konkola mines is seen as crucial to the rehabilitation of the mining industry -- once one of the biggest producers of copper and cobalt in the world but now only the seventh-biggest producer of copper.
